tasks.title: A
tasks.statement:
Introduction:

In addition to the beautiful physical landscapes, the citizens here also appreciate aspects of human
geography, particularly how their unique culture and values create a special type of urban landscape. In
a recent survey, Baie-Saint-Paul citizens voted the downtown area as the most representative landscape
of their region, and also one of their favourites. The local history of art is a key element of the cultural
heritage of the city, and forms the basis of the tourism industry.

Your task is:
    • to explore the downtown area by following the route drawn in red on Map A1
    • to complete an inventory of cultural heritage that reflects the art and historical culture that is so
        important to this city. (Map A2 – on a separate sheet)
    • to identify the areas that are not attractive and so reduce a tourist’s appreciation of the city’s
        culture and landscape. (Map A3).

Note – there is a large area to walk around, you must move quickly, but be safe and respectful of the
citizens and visitors to Baie-St-Paul. Cross only at crosswalks and watch for cars at all intersections.

General Instructions
    •   Before you start any field work task, read the instructions carefully and follow all instructions.
    •   Phones and cameras are NOT allowed on this day, and will be confiscated if found. We will be

    •   It is important if you usually carry medication you must bring this with you at all times during the

        with you.
    •   The test is individual.
    •   At no point will you be working together in a group.
FIELDWORK INSTRUCTIONS:

The fieldwork exercise consists of two parts, A and B, and they are at different sites.

Part A will be in an urban environment, and you will need to be careful when crossing streets and working
in crowded areas. All students will gather at one central location and be given common instruction. The
work is done individually and you may work and walk at your own pace. There is a lot of area to cover, so
be efficient with your time. Volunteers will be stationed along the route to ensure you stay in the fieldwork
area and to address any problems that may occur. YOU are responsible for your timing. Bring a watch if
you have one. You may also ask the volunteers for the time, and how much time is left. At the end of 75
minutes, you will be required to check-in at the start point or one other check point which will be
identified on your instructions.

Part B will take place in a natural area that has uneven terrain, tripping hazards and could be wet. Please
be careful at all times. You will have 75 minutes to walk around the site. YOU are responsible for your
timing. Bring a watch if you have one. You may also ask the volunteers for the time, and how much time
is left.

SCHEDULE:

You will start with either Part A or Part B in the morning. After lunch you will switch and go to the other
site. After the second site, all participants will then return back to Universite Laval.

You are responsible for your timing in the exercises. There will be volunteers around the field sites to
help keep you on track, but you are responsible for returning to the meeting points at the correct time. A
characteristic of a good field worker is the ability to stay focused and efficient in data collection, and
therefore, that is part of the Fieldwork Exercise.

Fieldwork Site Context

The area you are in, Charlevoix, is remarkable both geographically and historically. Geographically, you
are on the north shore of the St. Lawrence River, a key access point into Canada from the 1600s until
today. The region was designated a World Biosphere Reserve by UNESCO in 1989. The area’s elevation
ranges from 0-1150m above mean sea level, and is characterized by rolling hills, Canadian Shield (old
metamorphic bedrock), river ecosystems, estuarine tidal marshes and mud flats, mixed forest, boreal
forest, and alpine tundra.

Key faunal species include beluga whale and blue whale, wolf, caribou, moose, and cougar.

Historically, this was one of the first areas settled in Canada. The economy was originally water-based
(coastal navigation, fisheries). Today the economy is based on tourism and agro-forestry.

The diversity of land uses and the varied topography has resulted in an appealing landscape for artists.
This area is famous as an arts community and celebrates and supports a unique and rich visual arts
heritage. Recently the city of Baie-Saint-Paul adopted a policy aimed at promoting its rich heritage and
setting guidelines for its cultural development. It also adopted and put into action a sustainable
development policy. This series of initiatives earned it the title of Cultural Capital of Canada.

The City of Baie-Saint-Paul initiated a landscape plan this year. The goal of the plan is to identify local
landscapes that are valued by the citizens, understand the landscape qualities that are appealing, and
define specific goals and outcomes to ensure sustainable development of their landscapes. The first steps
in developing the plan are:

    1. Consultation with citizens through a survey
    2. Development of an initial landscape plan

The City sent out a survey to the citizens asking them to identify:

    1. their favourite landscapes
    2. the landscapes which best represent the area
    3. aspects of the landscape that are disliked

Today as part of the Fieldwork Test, you will explore two of these landscapes.

    1. The Boisé du Quai (coastal area), deemed the most favourite area, and the third most
       representative of the area.
    2. Downtown Baie-Saint-Paul, deemed the second favourite area, and was voted the most
       representative landscape of the area.

These two areas were also identified as important viewpoints in the area, indicating their uniqueness and
value to citizens and tourists.

tasks.title: Boisé du Quai – Bay Area
tasks.statement:
This task is worth 20 marks.

Instructions

The Bay area is the favourite landscape of the citizens of Baie-Saint-Paul. They want to develop the
recreation facilities and increase protection of the area.

Read the responses to the survey in Tables C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6 (pages 6 and 7).

Consider the citizens’ responses to the survey, and your own knowledge about the different
environments at this site.

1.    Design a land use plan for the Boisé du Quai area on the template map provided (Map C2 on a
     separate sheet) with the following considerations:
     a. It must reflect the goals of the community in both development and protection.
     b. It must allow people easily to access all the different landscapes at the site.
     c. It must include a heavy use recreational space.
     d. It must indicate which areas are most sensitive and need to be protected.

Sketch the features that your plan will include onto the template map (Map C2).

2. Annotate your suggestions to justify your choices. No additional text or writing is permitted.

END OF THE TEST
